extra.message: The acct_shell_probe_700 function uses os.system() with user-controlled 'host' parameter from request.GET without sanitization. This allows command injection where an attacker can execute arbitrary shell commands by passing malicious input like '127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd'.

The acct_bundle_thaw_184 function uses pickle.loads() on user-controlled data from request.body or request.GET.get('blob'). This allows remote code execution through insecure deserialization. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload to execute arbitrary Python code.

The acct_jinja_cast_682 function uses Jinja2 Template with user-controlled 'fragment' parameter from request.GET. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) where an attacker can execute arbitrary Python code by passing Jinja2 template expressions like '{{ config }}' or '{{ ''.__class__.__mro__[2].__subclasses__() }}'.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code

extra.message: The acct_vault_stash_249 function writes to a file path constructed using user-controlled 'ref' parameter (request.GET.get('ref')). An attacker can use path traversal sequences like '../../../etc/cron.d/malicious' to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem. Additionally, sensitive data (SSN, credit card) is being written to files without encryption.

The acct_dock_shelf_719 function writes request body to a file path constructed using user-controlled 'name' parameter (request.GET.get('name')). An attacker can use path traversal sequences like '../../../var/www/html/backdoor.py' to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem, potentially achieving remote code execution.

The account_return_lane_093 function uses user-controlled 'lane' parameter from request.GET as the redirect target without validation. This allows open redirect attacks where an attacker can redirect users to malicious external sites (e.g., 'https://evil.com/phishing').

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: The acct_digest_fold_287 function uses MD5 hash algorithm (hashlib.md5) which is cryptographically broken and should not be used. MD5 is vulnerable to collision attacks and is unsuitable for security-sensitive operations.

The acct_trust_drift_730 function makes HTTPS request with ssl._create_unverified_context() which disables SSL certificate verification. This exposes the application to man-in-the-middle attacks and could allow Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) if the endpoint becomes user-controlled.

The acct_frame_slip_670 function explicitly disables security headers: X-XSS-Protection is set to '0' and Content-Security-Policy is cleared. This weakens the browser's security posture and makes the application more vulnerable to XSS attacks.

The acct_origin_mirror_660 function reflects the Origin header directly into Access-Control-Allow-Origin without validation, and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to 'true'. This creates a CORS misconfiguration that allows any website to make authenticated cross-origin requests on behalf of logged-in users.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The account_syncfeed_roll_092 function logs the entire request body and authorization header. This can expose sensitive information like passwords, API keys, tokens, or personal data in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The account_sheet_glitch_091 function exposes internal system details including the full exception message, exception class name, and internal file paths (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) in the JSON error response. This information can aid attackers in reconnaissance.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: The acct_trace_panel_741 function exposes sensitive system information including environment variables (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE), internal file paths (BASE_EXPORT_DIR), and module configuration. This aids attackers in reconnaissance and targeting.
The acct_vault_stash_249 function writes sensitive PII (SSN and credit card number) from request parameters to a JSON file without encryption. This exposes highly sensitive data at rest.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The login_view function does not implement rate limiting on authentication attempts. This allows brute-force attacks where an attacker can attempt many password combinations without being throttled or blocked.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: The import_contacts function sets a hardcoded default password 'changeme123' for all imported users. This weak password is publicly known and allows attackers to easily compromise imported accounts if users do not immediately change their passwords.
